definition: Class inheritance is a feature in object-oriented programming that allows a class to inherit properties and behaviors (methods) from another class.
details: Class inheritance is a feature in object-oriented programming that allows a class to inherit properties and behaviors (methods) from another class. Referred to as a "subclass" or "derived class," the class that inherits is able to extend the functionality of the "base class" or "superclass."

explainer.lead: Class inheritance lets one class reuse the properties and methods defined by another, then add its own functionality. It gives programmers a way to express shared behavior once and build specialized versions without starting from scratch.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a recipe for a simple cake. A chocolate-cake recipe can start with everything in that recipe and add cocoa, instead of writing the whole thing again. Class inheritance works similarly: one blueprint for a program can reuse another blueprint’s information and actions, then add something extra.
tiers.practitioner: Define shared properties and methods in a base class, then declare a subclass and add only its specialized behavior. This is useful when several derived classes genuinely share the same base functionality. Changes to inherited behavior can affect every subclass, so the base abstraction and its assumptions should be kept clear.
tiers.paperLevel: Let B = (P_B, M_B) be a base class with properties P_B and methods M_B. A derived class D inherits P_B and M_B and may add extensions (P_D, M_D), making the inherited members and its additions available through D. B is the superclass or base class; D is the subclass or derived class.

explainer.example: A base class Account defines a balance property and a deposit() method. A derived class SavingsAccount inherits both and adds applyInterest(), so it can accept deposits through the inherited method while also providing its own interest-related behavior.

usedIn.name: Object-oriented software
usedIn.detail: Shares common properties and methods through base classes, then specializes them in derived classes.

usedIn.name: Reusable class design
usedIn.detail: Lets related subclasses extend one superclass instead of repeating its definitions.

explainer.intuition: Inheritance is like starting with an existing blueprint rather than a blank page: the subclass receives the base class’s features and can build on them.
howItWorks: Define shared properties and methods in a base class, also called a superclass.
Declare another class as its subclass, or derived class.
The subclass inherits the base class’s properties and behaviors.
Add new functionality to the subclass to extend what the base class provides.
explainer.whyItMatters: It supports reuse and extension: common functionality can be defined in a superclass, while each subclass supplies the additional behavior it needs.
misconceptions: A subclass is not merely a renamed copy; it inherits the base class’s features and can extend them.
Inheritance concerns class definitions, not copying data from one individual object into another.
